relations.myth: Colonial identification of Sumé with the traveling apostle
relations.note: Missionaries fused Sumé with Saint Thomas through names, footprints, teaching, and travel traditions.
Montoya portrays Sumé-Thomas as an apostolic missionary acting under Christian divine providence.

relations.myth: Campaign against evil and the seven monsters
relations.note: Tumé acts under Tupã’s superior authority and seeks divine aid against evil.

relations.myth: Tumé’s opposition to Taû and his monstrous offspring
relations.note: Wise Tumé ideologically and practically opposes Taû, Colmán’s embodiment of evil.

relations.myth: Campaign against Taû and Kerana’s offspring
relations.note: Tumé has an indirect adversarial relation with Kerana through the seven-monster cycle.
Tumé participates in the campaign against Teju Jagua and the other monstrous children.

relations.myth: Burning the monsters in Moñái’s cave
relations.note: Tumé and his people oppose the monsters gathered at Moñái’s cave and organize their destruction.
